result.title: METER: Matched-Event Calibration for Short-Event EEG Microstate Transition Analysis
result.comment: 36 pages. Supplementary material (16 pages) included as an ancillary file. Abdul Basit and Eklavya Tomar contributed equally
result.summary: Short cognitive events contain unequal and often sparse transition evidence, so raw EEG microstate distances can reflect finite sampling rather than neural reconfiguration. We introduce METER (Matched-Event Transition Estimation against a Reference), a participant-relative framework that separates marginal occupancy from conditional next-state choice and evaluates each event against duration-conditioned events from a fixed participant-specific reference bank. METER-Jump integrates uncertainty in sparse target and reference transition tables, returning a randomized event rank for testing and a continuous standardized coordinate for association analysis. Using a reproducible three-state representation selected by spatial criteria, we evaluated METER with participant-fitted simulations, estimator ablations, map perturbations, and preprocessing sensitivities. Event-level false-positive rates were 0.044-0.056 across four heterogeneous null mechanisms. By contrast, global cutoffs learned under the participant-fitted null and transferred unchanged to other regimes produced false-positive rates from 0.004 under rare transitions to 0.234 under map perturbation; duration-conditioned ranks remained near 0.05. Detection probability was approximately 0.69 with fixed maps but fell to 0.22 after bootstrap-derived map-assignment perturbation. In 4,175 natural-reading events from 18 participants, no linguistic association survived multiplicity correction in the primary 30-ms analysis, although a 20-ms sensitivity changed one within-stream max-$T$ decision. METER therefore calibrates finite-event departures conditional on a defined microstate sequence, while map assignment, filtering, temporal smoothing, and reference construction remain separate sources of measurement uncertainty.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 METER 框架，用被试自身、按时长条件匹配的参考事件库校准短时 EEG 微状态转移，区分边际占用与条件性下一状态选择，并结合稀疏转移表的不确定性给出随机化事件排名，在模拟与自然阅读数据中检验假阳性率与检出力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把状态转移与有限采样伪迹分离、并对转移表不确定性做校准的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态转移与轨迹相似度是否反映真实计算重配置而非样本量、噪声或扰动带来的假象。
